result.title: Does Learning Order Explain Forgetting? The Lie Bracket as an Early-Warning Signal for Catastrophic Forgetting Without Old Data
result.summary: A network trained on task A and then task B ends at different weights than one trained on B and then A. To leading order this gap is set by the Lie bracket of the two tasks' gradient fields, and Dherin (2023) conjectured that a non-vanishing bracket may be linked to catastrophic forgetting. I test this conjecture empirically. Across Split MNIST, Split Fashion-MNIST and Split CIFAR-10, the forgetting of A is almost exactly the difference in A's loss between the two training orders (Spearman rho = 0.96-1.00). I then ask whether the bracket can predict that forgetting early in training on B and without any of A's data, using only a small summary stored when A finishes: its gradient and its top 20 Hessian eigenpairs. When the old task is well learned and forgetting is slow (task-incremental), this stored bracket ranks forgetting with rho = 0.70-0.81, against 0.33-0.58 for the penalty of Elastic Weight Consolidation, and matches or exceeds re-evaluating A on its own data. When forgetting is fast (domain-incremental), the stored summary goes stale and the EWC penalty is as good or better. The bracket fails outright when the old task is only half learned; I trace this to a residual gradient on A an order of magnitude larger, which makes first-order (slope) damage matter. The bracket is therefore a useful early-warning signal for the quiet kind of forgetting, under a clear condition.

AI.brief_summary: 论文实证检验「两任务梯度场的 Lie bracket 非零与灾难性遗忘相关」这一猜想，在多个 Split 图像分类基准上比较训练顺序导致的损失差与遗忘，并尝试仅用旧任务结束时存储的梯度及 top-20 Hessian 特征对，在训练新任务早期预测遗忘。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关系，但「学习顺序—遗忘」及用旧任务低维摘要做无旧数据预警，可能为顺序训练 VLM 推理能力（如 THINK/LOOK 阶段）时的能力漂移监测提供概念线索；其依赖旧任务充分学习、任务增量等条件是否适用于 latent 推理状态仍待核查。
